newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coalition MPs give green light to Waigel's budget.
newsitem.headline: Coalition MPs give green light to Waigel's budget.

text.p: Parliamentary deputies in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition government on Thursday gave the green light to Finance Minister Theo Waigel's supplementary budget for 1997 and draft budget for 1998.
The deputies, voting in separate meetings of their parliamentary groups, gave their backing to the budgets as Waigel gets ready to present them to cabinet on Friday.

The supplementary budget for 1997 raises the deficit to 71 billion marks ($40.3 billion), much higher than an original plan for 53.3 billion. This will put the German deficit this year higher than public investment outlay, which is not constitutional.
In order to pass the budget anyway, the government must ask parliament to declare Germany's economy "out of balance" as a result of lower-than-expected tax revenues and high unemployment.
The draft budget for 1998 plans a deficit of just under 58 billion marks.
Parliamentary deputies appeared satisfied with the results of weeks of tough negotiations over the budget details.

Paul Krueger, a former research minister and east German deputy in Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party, said he could live with the cuts in aid to east Germany, but that there was still a need to discuss some minor details. ($ = 1.763 German Marks)
